newsitem.title: INDIA: India to hike gold import under special licenses.
newsitem.headline: India to hike gold import under special licenses.

text.p: The Indian government plans to allow higher imports of gold against special licenses, Commerce Secretary Tejendra Khanna said on Friday.
"In the short term, we shall increase entitlement of gold under special import licenses," Khanna told an econoomic conference of the World Gold Council (WGC) in New Delhi on Friday.
Khanna was respoonding to various demands made by the Indian gold industry and trade.
Khanna said bulk bullion imports by banks other than the State Bank of India (SBI) could also be considered.
The Indian commerce secretary ruled out free imports of gold (under an open general license).
"India will have to build up a level of $100 billion in exports and about $95 billion to $100 billion imports, then only gold import can be considered," Khanna said.
These figures are nearly thrice the value of India's exports and imports in financial year 1995/96 (April-March).
Indian exports in the last financial year stood at $31.83 billion and imports were $36.37 billion, according to official figures.
